targets: PostgreSQL 16.6 and 17.2, UTF-8, standard-conforming strings, native parameters
theorems: For each decoded name and a suffix whose first character is not the identifier quote, the scanner of the quoted name followed by this suffix returns the identical decoded name and suffix.

Every header and target of the stated arity round-trips under the fixed canonical REINDEX decoder. The command head preserves the exact selector, requested concurrency when applicable, and progress-reporting choice.
profileConditions: The accepted PostgreSQL Identifier contains a nonempty valid UTF-8 sequence without NUL and fits the 63-byte profile. The formal lexical result quantifies over all character lists.
PostgreSQL parses the fixed canonical syntax and counts each doubled identifier quote as one decoded character. Native name binding requires the same externally supplied identities.
The single named table syntax can refer to a standalone or partitioned owner. The separate IR role constrains which external owner is selected.
The command theorem applies to the branch without an explicit TABLESPACE destination. The identifier theorem also applies to the quoted destination name as an isolated option operand.
connection: Check the exact PHP branches for absent and present placement, the six canonical command selectors and all named operands. For an absent placement, the selected branch matches the unchanged canonical lexical model. The explicit placement prefix uses the same proved identifier encoding. The full header with placement is independently compared on stock releases.
proofValidation: Use a fixed trusted challenge export and compare both named theorem statements. Replay with Lean and at least one external kernel. Reject unapproved axioms, native computation axioms and mismatched theorem types. Record the exact verifier, source and artifact identity and actual availability of the sandbox.
measurement: Separate the universal lexical theorem from the native execution comparison. The theorem covers canonical tokenization and names. The PostgreSQL engine and source rule checks establish the bounded semantic report, storage and transaction observations.
rationale: Keep the theorem statements, definitions, solution and allowed dependencies fixed as the PHP publication gains a separate typed placement branch.
